subject.title: [Bug]: embedded prompt cache breaks across room-event, policy, and Responses boundaries

question: Should stable model-visible protected-tool schemas plus immutable pre-execution denial become the canonical authorization design across embedded, MCP, Codex, Copilot, and CLI paths?
rationale: The candidate moves authorization enforcement across several execution owners; automated review can verify the regression and dependency contract but cannot choose the permanent security-boundary design.

options.title: Adopt centralized policy
options.body: Approve stable schemas with deterministic per-turn policy snapshots and mandatory denial before hooks or side effects across every execution path.

options.title: Retain schema filtering
options.body: Keep unavailable protected tools hidden and accept prompt-cache churn while limiting the fix to reconstruction and continuation behavior.

options.title: Request a narrower redesign
options.body: Pause the candidate until a smaller authorization abstraction proves equivalent cache stability and cross-path safety.

recommendation.title: Adopt centralized policy
recommendation.body: Approve stable schemas with deterministic per-turn policy snapshots and mandatory denial before hooks or side effects across every execution path.

likelyOwner.reason: The current policy behavior traces directly to his recent commits on the central agent-tools and MCP paths.
